//: BuildSmart — Firestore composite indexes (launch Phase G · G1).
Project `buildsmart-b0b78`. Deploy:
firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project buildsmart-b0b78
(firebase.json now points firestore.indexes -> this file).
WHY composite indexes: a query that filters on one field AND orders by
another (or filters on two) needs a composite index — Firestore's automatic
single-field indexes do not cover those. See firestore.rules header 'RULES
ARE NOT FILTERS': a non-manager must SCOPE its listen, and those scoped
queries are exactly the ones indexed here.
Each index below, in order, and its uid-migration state (verified vs repo):
1. orders (contractorUid ASC, ts DESC) — LANDED (uid-A3, commit 24b5bc2).
The contractor scoped listen where('contractorUid'==uid).orderBy('ts'
desc) — newest-first own orders. ACTIVE NOW (contractorUid is written).
2. orders (storeId ASC, ts DESC) — FORWARD-READY. storeId not yet written
(orders_firebase toDoc omits it); ship so the store scoped listen lights
up the moment an A-phase stamps it (no second deploy / index-build wait).
3. orders (courierId ASC, ts DESC) — FORWARD-READY (same as storeId).
4. customers (ownerId ASC, used DESC) — FORWARD-READY. ownerId not yet
written; keeps the spend-desc order mgrCustomerList uses for the owner
scoped list once ownerId lands.
5. chatThreads (participants ARRAY_CONTAINS, ts DESC) — FORWARD-READY for
the post-S1 uid contract. participants today carries ROLE NAMES not uids
(S1 deferred), but the array-contains+orderBy shape is value-agnostic, so
it is correct to ship now. Query: where('participants', arrayContains:
uid).orderBy('ts' desc) (S4.1).
6. chatMessages (threadId ASC, ts ASC) — ACTIVE NOW. threadId IS written
today; the per-thread stream where('threadId'==id).orderBy('ts') (S4.2)
renders the conversation chronologically (ascending).
NOTE: `ts` is written as an ISO-8601 STRING (orders_firebase toDoc:
createdAt.toIso8601String()); ISO-8601 sorts lexicographically == chrono, so
a string-field DESC/ASC index orders correctly. fieldOverrides is left empty
— every collection keeps its automatic single-field indexes.
